beats.narration_text: Konnichiwa. This is Liam, in for Bear. With hundreds of tools, it's tempting to ask how to fit them all into Claude's context. But each one costs room before any work starts. So the real question is how to let Claude find the tools it needs.

beats.narration_text: A tool: a function Claude can ask your app to run. A definition: its name, what it does, and its inputs. Context: everything Claude reads, counted in tokens. And an embedding: numbers that place text by its meaning.

qc.sparse_reason: TERMS card: four prerequisites, one line each.

beats.narration_text: Say your app has hundreds of tools. Each has a definition: its name, what it does, and its inputs. Normally, every definition goes into Claude's context, on every request.

shot.visual_intent: Claude (a kraft block with a terracotta spark on a dark plinth) drops in at the left with its context tray, a low kraft open box ('Claude'); at the right a dark pegboard rises and fills with white tool cards row by row ('tools'); one card slides out and swells, and three grey bars draw on it (name, what it does, inputs) ('definition').
shot.motion_claim: Claude (a kraft block with a terracotta spark on a dark plinth) drops in at the left with its context tray, a low kraft open box ('Claude'); at the right a dark pegboard rises and fills with white tool cards row by row ('tools'); one card slides out and swells, and three grey bars draw on it (name, what it does, inputs) ('definition').

beats.narration_text: The context fills before work begins. Anthropic's cookbook says that past about a hundred tools, this becomes impractical: more cost, more time, and the right tool is harder to find.

shot.visual_intent: Card after card flies from the wall into the tray and a white pile grows past the tray's rim ('context'); the hero number lands above ('~100 tools', 'per Anthropic's cookbook').

show.event: every card goes into the tray

shot.motion_claim: Card after card flies from the wall into the tray and a white pile grows past the tray's rim ('context'); the hero number lands above ('~100 tools', 'per Anthropic's cookbook').

beats.narration_text: So Claude carries one tool instead: tool search. You still send every definition, but mark the rest defer loading. They stay out of Claude's context until a search finds them.

shot.visual_intent: The pile sinks out of the tray; one small kraft block with a dark lens and a terracotta light drops into the empty tray ('tool_search'); the wall's cards fade to ghost one row at a time ('deferred').

show.event: the tray empties; one tool lands

shot.motion_claim: The pile sinks out of the tray; one small kraft block with a dark lens and a terracotta light drops into the empty tray ('tool_search'); the wall's cards fade to ghost one row at a time ('deferred').

beats.narration_text: The cookbook searches by meaning. Each definition becomes text, and a small embedding model turns it into three hundred eighty-four numbers: a point on a map. Similar tools land close together.

shot.visual_intent: The wall shrinks to the top right; a pale kraft map plane on a dark plinth draws in below it ('map'); card after card drops from the wall onto the map and becomes an ink dot; the dots gather in clusters ('weather', 'finance').
shot.motion_claim: The wall shrinks to the top right; a pale kraft map plane on a dark plinth draws in below it ('map'); card after card drops from the wall onto the map and becomes an ink dot; the dots gather in clusters ('weather', 'finance').

beats.narration_text: Claude calls tool search in plain words, like the cookbook's test: I need to check the weather. The query lands on the same map, and the closest points come back: get weather, get forecast, air quality.

shot.visual_intent: A white query slip arcs from Claude down onto the map ('query') and becomes a terracotta dot inside the weather cluster; grey spokes draw from it to the three closest dots, which swell (three of the four weather dots; the fourth stays small) ('closest 3').
shot.motion_claim: A white query slip arcs from Claude down onto the map ('query') and becomes a terracotta dot inside the weather cluster; grey spokes draw from it to the three closest dots, which swell (three of the four weather dots; the fourth stays small) ('closest 3').

beats.narration_text: Your code sends back just their names. The API swaps each name for its full definition, and Claude calls get weather like any other tool. Tools it didn't find never entered its context.

shot.visual_intent: Three white name tags rise from the three winning dots and arc into the tray ('names'); in the tray each tag grows into a full white card beside tool_search ('definitions'); the first card gets an ink check; the ghost wall stays outside.

show.event: the API expands them into full cards

shot.motion_claim: Three white name tags rise from the three winning dots and arc into the tray ('names'); in the tray each tag grows into a full white card beside tool_search ('definitions'); the first card gets an ink check; the ghost wall stays outside.

beats.narration_text: You don't have to build the search yourself. The live docs offer a built-in tool search on Anthropic's side: one version matches patterns, one takes plain queries. The cookbook adds search by meaning.

shot.visual_intent: The map and cards clear; beside the kraft tool_search block, a dark block with two terracotta lights drops onto the tray ('built-in'); the kraft block gets a small map face ('custom'); from each, one card flies back from the wall to the tray.

show.event: the custom one searches by meaning

shot.motion_claim: The map and cards clear; beside the kraft tool_search block, a dark block with two terracotta lights drops onto the tray ('built-in'); the kraft block gets a small map face ('custom'); from each, one card flies back from the wall to the tray.

beats.narration_text: The docs suggest tool search from ten tools up. With fewer, or when every tool is used on every request, just load them. And keep your three to five most used tools loaded, ready without a search.

shot.visual_intent: A short row of four cards slides into the tray and fits, and an ink check lands ('10+ tools' sits over the wall as the threshold); the four leave, and three favourite cards settle in the tray beside tool_search for good ('always loaded'); the ghost wall stays deferred.
shot.motion_claim: A short row of four cards slides into the tray and fits, and an ink check lands ('10+ tools' sits over the wall as the threshold); the four leave, and three favourite cards settle in the tray beside tool_search for good ('always loaded'); the ghost wall stays deferred.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. In Claude Code, paste this. Read the live docs for the tool search tool. Then write a Python script with twenty mock tools, including get weather, all set to defer loading, plus a custom tool search that ranks them by embeddings. Ask about the weather in Tokyo and print each tool Claude calls, in order, with each call's input tokens. Then rerun it with all twenty loaded. Then check: did Claude call tool search before get weather? And did the first call use fewer input tokens than with all twenty loaded?
